lines: A pair of logistic maps iterating once per sample in their chaotic range, giving two related noise voltages
Sets the map's parameter across the chaotic band from 3.56 to 3.9, where the higher settings are the noisier
Moves the Y map's parameter above the X map's by up to a tenth, so the two outputs drift apart
Attenuates the voltage at the jack beneath it before it reaches the map's parameter
Modulates the map's parameter through the attenuator above it; ±5V here moves the parameter by up to a fortieth
Carries the first map, -5V to 5V, a fresh value every sample
Carries the second map, -5V to 5V, running the same equation with the offset added to its parameter
Note — the module runs at the sample rate with no filtering, so both outputs are broadband noise; the chaos knob near its bottom end gives the most structured result
Note — the two maps start from the same value and only separate because of the offset knob; with the offset at zero they track each other exactly

lines: An envelope shaped like a thrown object's flight, rising and falling as a parabola and able to bounce
Sets how hard the shot is thrown, which sets how long the flight lasts
Attenuates the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to the impulse knob
Sets how steeply the shot is thrown, from nearly flat at the bottom to nearly vertical at the top
Attenuates the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to the angle knob
Sets how hard the shot is pulled back down, which is what curves the flight
Attenuates the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to the gravity knob
Sets how much of the angle is kept on each bounce, so low settings make the bounces die away quickly
Attenuates the voltage at the jack beside it before it is added to the bounce knob
Switched on, the shot bounces when it lands instead of stopping
Fires a shot, and holding it down keeps firing a fresh one every sample
Modulates the impulse through the small knob beside it
Modulates the angle through the small knob beside it
Modulates the gravity through the small knob beside it
Modulates the bounce through the small knob beside it
Any voltage other than zero here fires a shot, and a voltage held high keeps firing fresh ones
Carries the flight as an audio signal, -5V to 5V, with the sign flipping on alternate bounces so the bounces read as a waveform
Carries the flight as a control voltage, 0V to 10V, the ordinary envelope output
Sends a 10ms pulse at 10V when a shot is fired and again each time the flight comes back to zero
Note — nothing happens until a shot is fired, by the shoot button or by a voltage at the trigger jack
Note — the four setting knobs are read only while a flight is under way; turning one between shots changes nothing until the next shot starts
Note — with bounce switched on the flight keeps rebounding for up to sixteen thousand bounces before it gives up, which at low bounce settings is a long tail of very short hops

lines: One cell of a Luci network: a ramp that runs from 0 to 1, fires a pulse on all four sides when it gets there and has its phase knocked about by pulses from its neighbours
Sends the ramp back to the start and fires the cell's pulse
A pulse here multiplies the cell's phase by the influence setting, which pulls the ramp back towards its start
Sets the cell's rate at a volt per octave from a base of about an eighth of a hertz; with nothing patched the ramp takes about eight seconds
Any voltage other than zero here throws the ramp to a random position and holds the audio output at 0V for that sample
Sets how much a neighbour's pulse moves this cell's phase, 0V leaving the phase at zero after a pulse and 10V leaving it almost untouched
Carries the ramp itself, -5V to 5V, rising from the bottom to the top over one cycle
Goes to 1V for one sample when the ramp reaches the top, for patching into a neighbouring cell
Note — with nothing patched the cell runs on its own, putting out a rising ramp about once every eight seconds; the frequency, influence and randomize jacks are what the Luci control modules are for
Note — the four side inputs are not edge detected: any voltage other than zero counts as a pulse, so a held high gate pulls the phase back on every sample
Note — all four trigger outputs carry exactly the same pulse, and the pulse is 1V rather than the usual 10V, which is what the other Luci modules expect
Note — the influence input comes up unpatched at 0V, which makes every incoming pulse reset the cell's phase to zero rather than nudge it

lines: A button that sends a voltage for randomising the phase of the Luci cells patched to it
Held down, sends a voltage from the output that throws a Luci cell's phase to a random position

Note — the button is not a trigger: while it is held the cells patched to it are randomised on every sample

LuciControlINFL.notes: The maker gave no name to any knob, jack or button on this module, so hovering one shows no tooltip at all. The process function reads params[INFLUENCE_FINE_INPUT] where it plainly meant inputs[INFLUENCE_FINE_INPUT]. That index is 1 and the module declares only one parameter, so the added term is a read past the end of the parameter list rather than any control; the jack on the panel does nothing. Input 0 is declared with no jack and cannot be reached either.
